clue.text: Such blows make things harder to change

explanation.surface: A remark that certain punches make things more difficult to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges THINGS HARDER, all twelve letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch thrown with the boxer's stronger right fist is called by that name.

clue.text: Music paper and magazine in US

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper
Time is a weekly American news magazine

explanation.surface: Some musical item, a newspaper and an American magazine listed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A syncopated piano style popular around 1900, associated with Scott Joplin.

clue.text: Presumption soldier, for example, can be courageous

explanation.surface: Cheek and a soldier together may make for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' means the soldier ant, not a person in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and chivalrous, a synonym for bold in the face of danger.

clue.text: Order for street cop kept under strict wraps

indicators.note: an order for these words means putting their letters into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions for a police officer on the beat that must be kept confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified at the highest level of secrecy, so hidden from nearly everyone.

clue.text: President's architectural brothers

explanation.surface: A president's family of architects.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'President's' stands for 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname shared by two American heads of state and, pluralised, by a famous Georgian building family.

clue.text: On South side of French waterway

explanation.surface: Something on the southern bank of a French canal.

clue.text: Person who's matter-of-fact about a record

parts.note: re is a short word meaning concerning or about
a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: Someone who is down-to-earth about a disc or document.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone practical who sees things as they are rather than as hoped.

clue.text: Twelve points they score together, badly beaten

bruised all over from a severe beating

explanation.surface: A team scores twelve points together while being thrashed.

clue.text: Cause of loss of standing for man in the field

definitions.meaning: if a ..., one falls over and loses one's footing

explanation.surface: Something that brings down a player standing in the outfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket names its fielding positions; this one is near the wicketkeeper on the leg side.

clue.text: Hail a Conservative leading the right

parts.note: a claim is a right or title to something

clue.text: Town giving poet precedence over economist

explanation.surface: A town naming honours a poet above an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: MILTON KEYNES is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned English new town in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Weak hand making section of course hard to negotiate

definitions.text: section of course hard to negotiate
definitions.meaning: on a motor-racing track, a tight S-bend that slows the cars

explanation.surface: A poor hand of cards makes a tricky bend in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge term for a trumpless hand, and a racing circuit's sharp double bend.

clue.text: Newspaper placed back here? Times readers may use it

explanation.surface: A newspaper is put behind this paper, which Times readers might pick up.

clue.text: Expert from a small part of France

parts.note: dept is the abbreviation of département, an administrative division of France

explanation.surface: A specialist comes from a little corner of France.

clue.text: Players' opponents once — they did a lot of running

definitions.text: they did a lot of running
definitions.meaning: the gentry ran estates and much of the country

explanation.walkthrough: Players were cricket's professionals; the amateurs had their own team name in the old fixture.

clue.text: Old garment being worn, or a short suit

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket of past centuries
a garment that is on is being worn

explanation.surface: An old jacket being worn, or perhaps a brief outfit.

clue.text: Relative absence of content in answer that's obscure

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the first and last letters of the word remain

clue.text: Valiant characters of newly independent state

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brave people from a country that has just gained freedom.

clue.text: Such a person may be about to swindle

definitions.text: Such a person may be about to swindle

parts.note: c is the abbreviation of circa, about
to rook is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: A con artist poised to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest person, a criminal or cheat who preys on victims.

clue.text: Old port afforded by rich, not poor

indicators.note: poor here signals the letters are put into a weak, altered arrangement

clue.text: Excel in non-patent work

parts.note: something not latent is out in the open, overt
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Shine in work that is out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or surpass, a synonym for outdo.

clue.text: Found lexicographer initially put animal in dictionary

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken
in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A dictionary compiler first entered an animal in the book.

clue.text: Aspiration in King's speech

definitions.meaning: Martin Luther King's 1963 speech is known by its repeated phrase 'I have a ...'

explanation.surface: A hope expressed in a royal address.

clue.text: Gallery rebuilt on a grand scale

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of the word are reconstructed in a new order

explanation.surface: An art gallery reconstructed on a big scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadly or extensively, to a great extent.

clue.text: One who enjoys solitude before being joined by child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A loner who used to enjoy being alone until a child arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse or hermit living apart.

clue.text: Creature putting a chap at ease, so to speak

parts.note: a chap is a man, so a man at ease

explanation.surface: An animal making a fellow feel relaxed, as one might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A large plant-eating sea mammal, the sea cow.

clue.text: Note skating skill in extremely risky manoeuvring

parts.note: B is a musical note
skill at the rink, coined on the model of seamanship

explanation.surface: A musical note on ice-skating prowess shows dangerous tactics.
